notes: Background: Solaris Echo is the API layer for several telco-grade customer care platforms; looking to replace a legacy NLU layer with an LLM-backed assistant.
Workflow: high-concurrency chat for tier-1 support + embeddings for knowledge retrieval across 50M lines of docs.
Targets: P99 latency < 500ms for short chat turns; throughput 2k concurrent user sessions; cost sensitivity moderate (telecom margins tight).
Security: must have SSO/SAML, audit logging, and option for data residency in US/EU. Preferred KMS integration but flexible if vendor provides strong controls.
Engagement summary:
- 2025-09-10: Intro call (AE Avery Chen) — product team described use case, initial sizing. Very interested in Dedicated for predictable throughput.
- 2025-10-02: Technical deep-dive (SE Rafael Ortiz) — discussed batching, caching, and KV cache persistence. Rafael demoed latency profiles with similar telco workload.
- 2025-11-12: Security questionnaire sent; Solaris security asked for SOC2 type II, ISO statement, and KMS partnership list.
- 2025-12-03: Pricing deck shared (drive link). Solaris asked for a 90-day POC with canary traffic and SLA for failover to hosted variants.

- 2026-01-21: Final alignment call (FF-2026-01-21-8342). Customer said: 'We need something that plugs in today — low lift for devs.' They were impressed by Redwood's runtime but concerned about integration timeline for Dedicated and custom routing.
Loss reason (summary): Solaris selected OpenAI direct API for initial roll-out. Primary factors called out by the buyer:
* Developer simplicity and speed to production — OpenAI SDK + broad ecosystem (partners, plugins) required less engineering lift.
* Brand comfort — procurement and platform teams had existing references for OpenAI and Anthropic; risk perceived as lower opting for a single vendor with established contracts.
* Procurement/budget constraints — hiring freeze and a directive to minimize vendor onboarding complexity pushed them to a direct-cloud small-spend approach this quarter.
* No clear internal champion willing to own a longer Dedicated rollout; platform team prioritized short-term unblock.

Sales notes / follow-ups done: Rafael provided workaround patterns for staged Dedicated adoption (start hosted → migrate to Dedicated), left a checklist for data residency controls. Avery maintained discounts but Solaris wanted 3rd-party proof points.

Open items preserved for re-engagement: watch for Solaris security attestation updates, monitor their POC feedback on hallucination/regression tolerance, check back if they hit latency/cost pain after first 90 days.

Suggested re-entry plan: automated alert to AE in 6 months, prepare a one-pager comparing cost/latency trade-offs (Redwood Dedicated vs OpenAI hosted) and a migration checklist for low-friction cutover.
Internal win/loss takeaways: emphasize faster developer onboarding docs, modular POC pattern (hosted compatibility shim), and faster handoff for security artifact requests.

- 'Team wants minimal ops in Q1 due to hiring freeze' — Infra lead
